metadata.title: Nasdaq edges higher as SK Hynix makes record-breaking debut

content.text:
1:45pm: SK Hynix stock pops
Stocks edged higher on Friday as shares of South Korean memory chip maker and Nvidia supplier SK Hynix surged more than 14% in their US market debut.
The company raised $26.5 billion in the largest US IPO by a foreign company, with SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won telling Bloomberg the chipmaker could eventually expand beyond selling memory chips to offering "memory as a service" as a new business model.
12:40pm: Oil set for weekly gain
Crude oil is set for a weekly gain of about 5% as renewed US-Iran strikes disrupt tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, fuelling concerns over potential global supply disruptions, according to Axel Rudolph, Chief Technical Analyst at IG.
"The oil price is on track for its first weekly gain in a month, rising by around 5% amid renewed US-Iran strikes which disrupt tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns over global energy supplies," Rudolph said.
"While negotiations between Washington and Tehran on a longer-term agreement remain ongoing, the International Energy Agency warns that a prolonged conflict could hinder efforts to rebuild global oil inventories, although record crude production from the UAE has helped to partially offset supply disruptions."
11:10am: Fed testimony, inflation and retail sales next week
Bank of America said markets will be watching a busy week of economic data and Federal Reserve commentary, with Fed Chair Warsh's semiannual testimony, June inflation data and retail sales figures set to take centre stage.
The bank said Warsh's remarks on Tuesday will be closely scrutinized for clues on the Fed's policy outlook, alongside the release of June consumer price index (CPI) data. June producer prices, due Wednesday, will provide further insight into inflation trends ahead of the Fed's July meeting and help refine expectations for the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) inflation measure.
Investors will also assess the health of the US consumer through Thursday's retail sales report, while other releases including industrial production, housing starts and building permits, and the preliminary July University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey will provide additional signals on economic momentum.
A number of Fed officials are also scheduled to speak throughout the week, including Waller, Goolsbee, Williams, Musalem, Logan and Jefferson.
10:00am: Investors welcome SK Hynix IPO
Wall Street opened little changed on Friday as investors took a breather following this week's rally, with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq on track for modest weekly gains while the Dow looked set to finish the week largely flat.
